context_requirements: Expression of nuclear progesterone receptor (PGR) or other steroid receptors (ESR1, AR, NR3C1) that progestins can cross-activate
Hormone-responsive transcriptional machinery; PR-negative lines such as A549, PC3 and HT29 are expected to respond weakly or not at all
For antiproliferative effects, cells must be actively cycling and dependent on cyclin D1/CDK4-6 activity
falsifiers: No change in any of the listed PR/steroid-receptor target genes (FKBP4, TSC22D3, SGK1) at 6 h in MCF7 or other receptor-positive lines
No reduction in cyclin D1 (CCND1) or other proliferation genes at 24 h in any line
Strong, uniform transcriptional responses across all nine lines including receptor-negative lines, which would suggest a non-receptor-mediated off-target effect
Predominant induction of generic stress programs (unfolded protein response, heat shock, oxidative stress) rather than receptor-dependent transcriptional changes

evidence.supports: Ligand-bound progesterone receptor interacts with ER and reprograms ER transcriptional activity; megestrol plus letrozole reduced proliferation and ER genomic binding in ER+ breast cancer
Progesterone receptor agonist dienogest and progesterone inhibit proliferation of endometrial epithelial cells with suppression of cyclin D1 (CCND1) expression
Dienogest regulates apoptosis, proliferation and invasiveness of endometriotic stromal cells via endoplasmic reticulum stress induction
5alpha-dihydroprogesterone acts as a potent endogenous progesterone receptor agonist supporting progesterone-dependent gene expression
Progestin signaling through membrane progesterone receptors can inhibit apoptosis, a non-genomic PR pathway
